title: Inference blame-distribution and recovery canvas
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Build a comprehensive dashboard and taxonomy that attributes inference errors to root causes (network, overload, model, infra, client) and exposes recovery actions with playbook links.
description: Problem: We see frequent tail incidents in the inference path with mixed signals across traces, metrics and logs. Current dashboards show counts and 95/99 latencies but do not reliably attribute incidents to a single root cause or recommend immediate remediation. Goal: Deliver a blame-distribution dashboard and an operational recovery canvas that (1) classifies each failure event into a small set of canonical causes (network_timeout, overload_backpressure, model_exec_error, upstream_5xx, client_abort), (2) surfaces per-route and per-hardware exposure to SLIs, and (3) ties suggested mitigations (route-level fallback, autoscale, model-variant failover, retry policy) to the taxonomy so on-call can act quickly.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical failure tag (failure_cause) is added to enriched spans and log events with values: network_timeout, overload, model_error, upstream_error, client_cancel, unknown
Dashboard panels: top-10 failure vectors by volume and by SLI-exposure; blame waterfall showing proportional contribution of each cause to SLO breaches
Per-route SLI exposure heatmap (region x backend-pool x model_variant) with drilldown to sample traces
Automated playbook links for top-3 causes visible on dashboard; each link contains remediation steps and corresponding runbook PR
Sampling policy implemented: 1% baseline full-trace sampling, ramp to 100% for events tagged failure_cause!=unknown for 2 minutes post spike
Log/metric schema change is backwards-compatible; data backfills for 30 days available in analytics store
Unit and integration tests for trace hook enrichment and pipeline transform merged to main.
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff with Observability, SRE and Runtime teams. Agreed on canonical cause set and attributes to attach to spans (failure_cause, failure_subtype, inferred_blame_score).

2025-01-20: Prototype tagging in local runtime branch. Added deterministic rule: if model returns non-2xx inference status -> model_error; if grpc deadline exceeded -> network_timeout. Initial unit tests pass.

2025-01-28: Trade-off discussion: high-cardinality failure_subtype (device_id, kernel) provides diagnostic value but increases cardinality in metrics storage. Decided to limit metrics to failure_cause and keep failure_subtype in logs only.

2025-02-01: PR opened for trace hook enrichment + sampling changes: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1826. Implementation uses a lightweight scorer that computes blame_score from tags and resource signals.
2025-02-03: Vector pipeline transform added to tag logs with failure_cause and route metadata. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4093. Waiting on staging tests (ETL/analytics).

2025-02-05: Dashboard wireframes reviewed with PM and SRE. Feedback: include quick actions (trigger model-variant fallback, reroute to dedicated pool) and link to canary rollouts. Design will be implemented in console-2025.03 workstream.

2025-02-07: Addressed initial review comments on PR: reduced default trace sample rate, added feature flag for aggressive sampling. Next: complete pipeline integration tests and create runbook drafts.
design_decisions: Keep blame taxonomy intentionally small (<=6 causes) so dashboard aggregation is stable and actionable
Make failure_cause a single-valued tag used for metric rollups; keep failure_subtype as free-text in logs for debuggability
Prefer heuristic scoring over ML for initial rollout to keep explainability and ease of audit
Sampling bump strategy: short window high-fidelity capture on anomalies to limit cost while preserving signal
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument runtime trace hooks to emit failure_cause and blame_score during response handling
2) Add vector transform to map runtime tags into structured log fields and forward to BigQuery/ClickHouse
3) Implement sampling controller: baseline 1% full traces, ramp based on failure tags
4) Build dashboard panels in console: (a) Blame waterfall, (b) SLI exposure heatmap, (c) Top failure vectors and suggested actions
5) Wire quick-action endpoints to initiate known remediations (fallback, reroute, autoscale override)
6) Run staging load tests and validate no regression in latency or cost
tradeoffs_and_risks: Increased trace/log volume during spikes could push observability costs; mitigated via short sampling windows and retention rules
Heuristic-based attribution may misclassify complex multi-hop failures; plan periodic review of misclassifications and adjustment rules
Cardinality of route/model_variant dimensions must be monitored or metrics rollups will explode storage costs
Quick-actions introduce operational risk if misused; require RBAC gating and confirmation dialogs
next_steps: Finish pipeline integration tests (platform PR) and validate backfill availability
Complete dashboard implementation and enable feature flag in staging for smoke tests
Draft runbooks for top-3 causes and link to quick-actions
Schedule on-call tabletop exercise to validate remediation UX
